# @clossys/designer/tokens

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-token-docs.mjs (repository tooling, not shipped). Edit shared token data, then regenerate. -->

The flat registry contains 217 stable CSS properties. This reference groups them into 9 display groups and 37 display families for navigation. The 31 source families remain compatibility and provenance data; a display group does not imply a value type or a usage.

Each property has zero per-token configuration. Brand and supported theme overlays resolve the same property identity. The inspector is named **Token details**; configurable components start at Atoms. Existing legacy `oldGroup.sourceFamily@token` references and bookmarks keep their original identity. Display regrouping does not rename those references.

Purpose, appropriate use, misuse, application context and specimen kind come from shared `TOKEN_GUIDANCE`. The explicit navigation tree is `TOKEN_DISPLAY_GROUPS`. Consumers import these records rather than maintain their own guidance. Default, source family, brandability and theme dependence below come directly from `TOKENS`; equal values and aliases do not make semantic roles interchangeable.

TokenDefinition retains 5 fields: `property`, `family`, `value`, `brandable`, `themeDependent`. The property remains the stable identity while its supported brand and theme bindings resolve.

## Install and bind

```bash
npm install @clossys/designer
```

```css
@import "@clossys/designer/tokens.css";
@import "./brand.css";
```

Start a brand overlay from `@clossys/designer/brand-template.css` and bind only slots that TOKENS marks brandable. Set `data-brand-bound` on the document root after supplying the real overlay. Non-brandable structural tokens retain their shipped contract. Use the brand-coverage and contrast gates documented in [README.md](README.md); a filled slot does not itself prove readable contrast.

Theme-dependent properties have light and dark declarations. Invariant aliases can still change appearance through their referenced property. A runtime CSS custom-property override cannot change a media query already compiled by Tailwind: breakpoint values are build-time thresholds, and native media conditions do not accept var().

## Read Token details

```ts
import { TOKENS, TOKEN_GUIDANCE, TOKEN_DISPLAY_GROUPS } from "@clossys/designer/tokens";

const property = "--color-surface-raised";
const definition = TOKENS[property];
const guidance = TOKEN_GUIDANCE[property];
console.log(definition?.value, guidance?.purpose, TOKEN_DISPLAY_GROUPS.length);
```

Application type describes the consuming CSS syntax, not a new field on TokenDefinition. A binding below is an application example, not proof that every component consumes that property. The actual resolved value depends on the supported brand and theme cascade. Check the named context before selecting an equal-valued alternative.

## Token reference

### Color

#### Surface (9)

##### `--color-surface-base`

- Purpose: The default ground establishes the page's normal reading plane.
- Appropriate use: Paint the document or a normal section on the base ground with its paired ink.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use base as a raised card cue; choose surface-raised for that relationship.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-surface-base)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Page and ordinary section backgrounds; verify ink contrast on this ground.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(0.9702 0 0)`. Source family: `surface`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-surface-sunken`

- Purpose: The recessed ground separates an inset region from the page plane.
- Appropriate use: Set a well, code recess or nested tray on the sunken surface.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid using sunken as disabled opacity; the alpha token controls transparency instead.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-surface-sunken)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Inset containers behind content, with foreground contrast checked separately.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(0.9401 0 0)`. Source family: `surface`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-surface-raised`

- Purpose: The raised ground gives a card or floating plate its own reading plane.
- Appropriate use: Use raised behind content that must separate from the base without reversing polarity.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not substitute the fixed neutral ramp for raised; this semantic surface follows its overlay.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-surface-raised)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Cards and raised content plates, paired with normal primary and secondary ink.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(1 0 0)`. Source family: `surface`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-surface-inverse`

- Purpose: The inverse ground establishes an intentionally opposite-polarity band.
- Appropriate use: Put an inverse section behind on-inverse ink and matching inverse controls.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid placing ordinary primary ink on inverse; choose the paired inverse foreground.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-surface-inverse)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Authored inverse sections; inverse is a role rather than an instruction to follow the OS theme.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(0.2178 0 0)`. Source family: `surface`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-surface-inverse-raised`

- Purpose: An inverse raised plate separates nested content inside an inverse band.
- Appropriate use: Use this plate when an inverse-ground card needs elevation within that same polarity.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not replace the outer inverse band with its raised child surface indiscriminately.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-surface-inverse-raised)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Nested plates on inverse surfaces with on-inverse foregrounds.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(0.285 0 0)`. Source family: `surface`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-surface-aside`

- Purpose: The aside ground distinguishes persistent supporting chrome from main content.
- Appropriate use: Apply aside behind a sidebar or supplementary reading region.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not treat aside as a modal scrim; overlay-scrim dims content behind a transient layer.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-surface-aside)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Persistent supporting regions, preserving the normal ink contrast relationship.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(0.9612 0 0)`. Source family: `surface`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-surface-selected`

- Purpose: The selected wash marks an item's persistent selection state.
- Appropriate use: Use selected behind the currently selected row or navigable item.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid using the selection wash as a generic hover fill; control-tonal-hover describes interaction.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-surface-selected)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Selection backgrounds whose meaning is also exposed by text, shape or state semantics.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(0.4748 0 0 / 0.1)`. Source family: `surface`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-surface-glass`

- Purpose: The normal glass plate keeps scrolled overlay-header content legible over imagery.
- Appropriate use: Use the normal glass surface with normal ink and the glass backdrop blur.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not assume translucent glass guarantees contrast over every image; test the composite.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-surface-glass)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Normal-polarity overlay header plates composited above a real backdrop.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(1 0 0 / 0.6)`. Source family: `surface`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-surface-glass-inverse`

- Purpose: The inverse glass plate preserves inverse-header polarity over moving page content.
- Appropriate use: Pair inverse glass with on-inverse ink when a scrolled overlay header gains a plate.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid mixing inverse glass with normal header ink; use the matching normal glass pair.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-surface-glass-inverse)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Inverse-polarity overlay header plates; composite contrast remains context dependent.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(0.2178 0 0 / 0.85)`. Source family: `surface`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

#### Ink (7)

##### `--color-ink-primary`

- Purpose: Primary ink carries the content a reader must notice and read first.
- Appropriate use: Use primary for normal-ground body copy, headings and essential labels.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not dim essential copy with a fixed neutral shade; muted ink has a separate contrast budget.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-ink-primary)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Text and meaningful foregrounds on normal semantic surfaces.
- Specimen kind: `text`.
- Default: `oklch(0.2178 0 0)`. Source family: `ink`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-ink-secondary`

- Purpose: Secondary ink lowers emphasis for supporting readable information.
- Appropriate use: Use secondary for explanatory copy adjacent to primary information.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use secondary to communicate a link merely because its default matches link ink.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-ink-secondary)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Supporting text on normal grounds; verify the declared text-size contrast threshold.
- Specimen kind: `text`.
- Default: `oklch(0.36 0 0)`. Source family: `ink`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-ink-muted`

- Purpose: Muted ink reserves lower emphasis for tertiary annotations.
- Appropriate use: Use muted for captions or metadata that remain readable at their actual rendered size.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid muted for critical instructions or disabled-state simulation; retain required contrast.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-ink-muted)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Tertiary normal-ground annotations, with a stricter check before using small type.
- Specimen kind: `text`.
- Default: `oklch(0.54 0 0)`. Source family: `ink`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-ink-link`

- Purpose: Link ink identifies a textual navigation action on normal ground.
- Appropriate use: Apply link ink to an actual link alongside an underline or another non-color cue.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not equate link and secondary roles when they resolve to the same starting value.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-ink-link)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Inline and standalone text links on normal surfaces, including visited and focus considerations.
- Specimen kind: `text`.
- Default: `oklch(0.36 0 0)`. Source family: `ink`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-ink-on-inverse`

- Purpose: On-inverse ink carries essential content on the inverse ground.
- Appropriate use: Pair this foreground with inverse surfaces for headings, body copy and key labels.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid placing on-inverse ink on the ordinary base ground; switch polarity as a pair.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-ink-on-inverse)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Primary text and meaningful symbols on inverse surfaces.
- Specimen kind: `text`.
- Default: `oklch(0.9702 0 0)`. Source family: `ink`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-ink-on-inverse-muted`

- Purpose: Muted inverse ink creates a supporting text tier inside an inverse band.
- Appropriate use: Use it for secondary annotations beside stronger on-inverse content.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not borrow ordinary muted ink for inverse annotations; its contrast relationship is different.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-ink-on-inverse-muted)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Supporting inverse-ground text, checked at its real font size.
- Specimen kind: `text`.
- Default: `oklch(0.7763 0 0)`. Source family: `ink`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-ink-on-accent`

- Purpose: On-accent ink supplies the foreground of a solid accent action.
- Appropriate use: Pair it with accent-filled buttons or badges after checking their resolved contrast.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use accent-text on a solid accent fill merely because both names mention accent.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-ink-on-accent)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Text or symbols on a solid accent surface; aliasing does not erase this role.
- Specimen kind: `text`.
- Default: `var(--color-ink-on-inverse, oklch(0.9702 0 0))`. Source family: `ink`. Brandable: no. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

#### Line (4)

##### `--color-line-base`

- Purpose: The base line separates ordinary neighboring surfaces without strong emphasis.
- Appropriate use: Use it for normal dividers and neutral control boundaries.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not rely on a faint base divider alone to communicate an interactive or invalid state.
- CSS binding: `border-color: var(--color-line-base)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Normal-ground separators; essential component boundaries need their own contrast check.
- Specimen kind: `border`.
- Default: `oklch(0.8761 0 0)`. Source family: `line`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-line-strong`

- Purpose: The strong line makes a boundary more explicit than the base divider.
- Appropriate use: Choose it when a normal-ground edge needs stronger visual definition.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid thickening every divider to compensate for weak color; border width and line role are separate.
- CSS binding: `border-color: var(--color-line-strong)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Emphasized normal-ground rules and component edges.
- Specimen kind: `border`.
- Default: `oklch(0.7763 0 0)`. Source family: `line`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-line-on-inverse`

- Purpose: The inverse line separates content within an inverse-polarity region.
- Appropriate use: Use this translucent line on inverse backgrounds with matching inverse ink.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not apply the inverse line to a light page and expect the same visibility.
- CSS binding: `border-color: var(--color-line-on-inverse)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Borders and separators composited on inverse surfaces.
- Specimen kind: `border`.
- Default: `oklch(0.9702 0 0 / 0.14)`. Source family: `line`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-line-panel`

- Purpose: The panel line owns the authored outline of cards and product panels.
- Appropriate use: Pair panel line with the panel border-width and corner tokens.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid replacing every ordinary divider with panel line; panel identity is a narrower role.
- CSS binding: `border-color: var(--color-line-panel)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Outlined card or panel edges, independent of panel shadow.
- Specimen kind: `border`.
- Default: `var(--color-line-base, oklch(0.8761 0 0))`. Source family: `line`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

#### Accent (5)

##### `--color-accent`

- Purpose: The solid accent establishes the strongest branded action fill.
- Appropriate use: Use accent behind a primary action with on-accent foreground contrast verified.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use the solid action fill as small text ink; accent-text is the text-oriented role.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-accent)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Primary action backgrounds and intentional accent fills.
- Specimen kind: `control`.
- Default: `oklch(0.4748 0 0)`. Source family: `accent`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-accent-text`

- Purpose: Accent text emphasizes a branded foreground while preserving text contrast.
- Appropriate use: Use accent-text for branded text or meaningful symbols on a normal surface.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid assuming the accent action fill is also suitable for small text; check this foreground pair.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-accent-text)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Normal-ground accent foregrounds at their actual text or icon size.
- Specimen kind: `text`.
- Default: `oklch(0.36 0 0)`. Source family: `accent`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-accent-hover`

- Purpose: The accent hover fill gives a solid accent action its pointer-hover response.
- Appropriate use: Apply it to the hover state of an already accent-filled action.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use hover fill as the default selected state or as a universal focus indicator.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-accent-hover)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Transient hover feedback for solid accent controls; keyboard focus needs its own cue.
- Specimen kind: `control`.
- Default: `oklch(0.36 0 0)`. Source family: `accent`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-accent-tint`

- Purpose: The accent tint supplies a low-emphasis branded wash.
- Appropriate use: Use the tint behind a callout or selected accent treatment with readable foreground ink.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not expect an accent wash to carry readable text by itself; pair an appropriate ink token.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-accent-tint)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Subtle accent backgrounds whose final appearance depends on the ground underneath.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(0.4748 0 0 / 0.1)`. Source family: `accent`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-accent-on-inverse`

- Purpose: Inverse accent ink retains branded emphasis against an inverse ground.
- Appropriate use: Use this foreground for accent links or symbols inside an inverse section.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid reusing normal accent-text on inverse solely because both are branded foregrounds.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-accent-on-inverse)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Branded foreground emphasis paired with inverse semantic surfaces.
- Specimen kind: `text`.
- Default: `oklch(0.7763 0 0)`. Source family: `accent`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

#### Control (5)

##### `--color-control-tonal`

- Purpose: The normal tonal fill distinguishes a low-emphasis action from its surrounding ground.
- Appropriate use: Use it as the resting fill of a tonal control on a normal surface.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use tonal fill for a content card or permanent selection; those have surface roles.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-control-tonal)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Normal-ground tonal controls; the translucent fill composites with their surrounding surface.
- Specimen kind: `control`.
- Default: `oklch(0.2178 0 0 / 0.08)`. Source family: `control`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-control-tonal-hover`

- Purpose: The normal tonal hover wash strengthens an existing tonal action under the pointer.
- Appropriate use: Use this fill only for the hover response of a normal-ground tonal control.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid treating tonal-hover as the resting fill of every secondary action.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-control-tonal-hover)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Pointer hover within the normal tonal tier, preserving a separate keyboard focus cue.
- Specimen kind: `control`.
- Default: `oklch(0.2178 0 0 / 0.12)`. Source family: `control`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-control-tonal-inverse`

- Purpose: The inverse tonal fill separates a quiet filled action from an inverse band.
- Appropriate use: Use inverse tonal with on-inverse foregrounds for an inverse-ground secondary action.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not apply the normal tonal fill to inverse and expect equivalent compositing.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-control-tonal-inverse)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Resting tonal controls on inverse semantic surfaces.
- Specimen kind: `control`.
- Default: `oklch(0.9702 0 0 / 0.12)`. Source family: `control`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-control-tonal-inverse-hover`

- Purpose: The inverse tonal hover wash strengthens an inverse action during pointer interaction.
- Appropriate use: Use it as the hover fill over the inverse tonal resting state.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid applying inverse tonal-hover to normal surfaces or using it as a persistent active state.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-control-tonal-inverse-hover)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Transient pointer feedback on inverse-ground tonal controls.
- Specimen kind: `control`.
- Default: `oklch(0.9702 0 0 / 0.16)`. Source family: `control`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-control-quiet`

- Purpose: Quiet control ink identifies a text-led action without adding a fill.
- Appropriate use: Use it for the label or chevron of a quiet control on its supported normal ground.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not assume every text button should look like a content link; quiet control and link roles differ.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-control-quiet)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Quiet action foregrounds; the alias follows primary ink unless a brand binds it differently.
- Specimen kind: `control`.
- Default: `var(--color-ink-primary, oklch(0.2178 0 0))`. Source family: `control`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

#### Status (12)

##### `--color-status-success`

- Purpose: The success mark color signals successful completion through a status symbol or fill.
- Appropriate use: Use the success mark for a completed operation or a confirmed healthy state, with a label or symbol carrying the meaning too.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use the success mark for an action that has not actually completed; it is not a generic text foreground.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-status-success)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Success status marks and fills, with non-color meaning and explicit foreground contrast.
- Specimen kind: `status`.
- Default: `oklch(0.6268 0 0)`. Source family: `status`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-status-success-text`

- Purpose: The success text ink makes a message about successful completion readable.
- Appropriate use: Use success text for the written status label beside its matching mark or wash.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not substitute the success mark fill for small status text without checking contrast.
- CSS binding: `color: var(--color-status-success-text)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Readable success message foregrounds on their declared ground or matching tint.
- Specimen kind: `status`.
- Default: `oklch(0.4748 0 0)`. Source family: `status`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-status-success-tint`

- Purpose: The success tint creates a supporting background for successful completion.
- Appropriate use: Place a success message on this wash while keeping its matching text and label explicit.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use the success wash alone to communicate state or as a replacement for the mark.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-status-success-tint)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Subtle success message backgrounds; test the translucent composite with its text ink.
- Specimen kind: `status`.
- Default: `oklch(0.6268 0 0 / 0.1)`. Source family: `status`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-status-warning)`. Application type: `color`.

- Default: `oklch(0.4495 0 0)`. Source family: `status`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

##### `--color-status-warning-tint`

#### Overlay (3)

##### `--color-overlay-surface`

- Purpose: The overlay surface gives transient content its shared reading plate.
- Appropriate use: Use the overlay plate behind menus, popovers, tooltips or other transient content.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not infer stacking order from this color; the relevant z token positions the layer.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-overlay-surface)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Transient content plates; the raised-surface alias preserves the overlay role.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `var(--color-surface-raised, oklch(1 0 0))`. Source family: `overlay`. Brandable: no. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

##### `--color-overlay-border`

- Purpose: The overlay border defines the edge of transient content plates.
- Appropriate use: Pair this edge with the overlay surface rather than a permanent panel identity.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use overlay border to darken the page behind a dialog; overlay-scrim does that.
- CSS binding: `border-color: var(--color-overlay-border)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Edges of transient overlays on the appropriate surrounding surface.
- Specimen kind: `border`.
- Default: `var(--color-line-base, oklch(0.8761 0 0))`. Source family: `overlay`. Brandable: no. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

##### `--color-overlay-scrim`

- Purpose: The overlay scrim subdues the underlying page while a modal layer takes attention.
- Appropriate use: Place the scrim between background content and a blocking dialog or drawer.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not put text directly on the scrim or use it as a general glass-header plate.
- CSS binding: `background-color: var(--color-overlay-scrim)`. Application type: `color`.
- Context: Full-backdrop modal dimming; modal semantics and focus management remain component behavior.
- Specimen kind: `surface`.
- Default: `oklch(0 0 0 / 0.4)`. Source family: `overlay`. Brandable: no. Theme-dependent declaration: yes.

### Typography

#### Font families (3)

##### `--font-display`

- Purpose: The display family establishes the brand's expressive large-type voice.
- Appropriate use: Use the display family for authored display headings through the shared font-display utility.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not replace body typography with display styling throughout a reading passage.
- CSS binding: `font-family: var(--font-display)`. Application type: `font-family`.
- Context: Display headings; the shared utility also consumes the display style, weight, stretch and scale settings.
- Specimen kind: `font`.
- Default: `system-ui, ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. Source family: `font`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

##### `--font-body`

- Purpose: The body family provides the default voice for sustained reading and interface copy.
- Appropriate use: Use the body family for paragraphs, ordinary headings and UI labels unless the type record assigns another role.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid choosing the body face independently in each component; bind it once in the brand overlay.
- CSS binding: `font-family: var(--font-body)`. Application type: `font-family`.
- Context: Reading text and ordinary interface copy governed by the brand type record.
- Specimen kind: `font`.
- Default: `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. Source family: `font`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

##### `--font-mono`

- Purpose: The mono family gives code and aligned technical text a consistent fixed-width voice.
- Appropriate use: Use the mono family for code, machine identifiers or tabular technical content when its metrics are needed.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use mono merely to shrink copy or bypass the reserved roles in the type record.
- CSS binding: `font-family: var(--font-mono)`. Application type: `font-family`.
- Context: Code and explicitly reserved technical text, with the mono role checked by the type record.
- Specimen kind: `font`.
- Default: `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`. Source family: `font`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

#### Display font settings (4)

##### `--font-display-style`

- Purpose: The display style selects the upright or slanted stance of the display face.
- Appropriate use: Bind display style to the actual supported style of the chosen display font.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not simulate an unsupported italic face or change body text style through this display-only setting.
- CSS binding: `font-style: var(--font-display-style)`. Application type: `font-style`.
- Context: The font-display utility's font-style declaration, separate from display weight and width.
- Specimen kind: `font`.
- Default: `normal`. Source family: `font`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

##### `--font-display-weight`

- Purpose: The display weight controls the stroke weight of the expressive display face.
- Appropriate use: Choose a supported display-face weight in the brand type record and bind that choice here.
- Misuse or alternative: Avoid compensating for an unsuitable font size by arbitrarily making every display heading heavier.
- CSS binding: `font-weight: var(--font-display-weight)`. Application type: `font-weight`.
- Context: The font-display utility's font-weight declaration, requiring the corresponding font resource.
- Specimen kind: `font`.
- Default: `400`. Source family: `font`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

##### `--font-display-stretch`

- Purpose: The display stretch selects a supported width variant of the display font.
- Appropriate use: Use this setting when the actual font offers the desired condensed or expanded width.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not assume font-stretch geometrically scales every installed font; scale-x is a different mechanism.
- CSS binding: `font-stretch: var(--font-display-stretch)`. Application type: `font-stretch`.
- Context: The font-display utility's font-stretch declaration; availability depends on the selected font.
- Specimen kind: `font`.
- Default: `100%`. Source family: `font`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

##### `--font-display-scale-x`

- Purpose: Display horizontal scale adjusts the rendered width of expressive display letterforms.
- Appropriate use: Use the shared display utility when the authored identity deliberately scales the display face horizontally.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not use horizontal scaling as responsive layout or assume a transform changes the element's layout width.
- CSS binding: `transform: scaleX(var(--font-display-scale-x))`. Application type: `number`.
- Context: A scaleX transform in the font-display utility; transformed containing-block behavior still applies.
- Specimen kind: `font`.
- Default: `1`. Source family: `font`. Brandable: yes. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

#### Font sizes (13)

##### `--text-display-xl`

- Purpose: The display-xl rung supplies the largest display statement in the fixed type scale.

### Responsive

#### Breakpoints (6)

##### `--breakpoint-mobile`

- Purpose: The mobile breakpoint supplies the compact mobile reference threshold.
- Appropriate use: Use breakpoint-mobile as a build-time minimum-width threshold for an authored smallest mobile layout transition.
- Misuse or alternative: Do not treat breakpoint-mobile as a guarantee that devices narrower than the reference cannot visit.
- CSS binding: `@media (min-width: 375px)`. Application type: `length`.
- Context: The mobile build-time media-query threshold; CSS var() cannot parameterize a native media condition.
- Specimen kind: `breakpoint`.
- Default: `375px`. Source family: `breakpoint`. Brandable: no. Theme-dependent declaration: no.

- Purpose: The mobile-lg breakpoint supplies the wider mobile reference threshold.

- Misuse or alternative: Do not treat breakpoint-mobile-lg as a synonym for the tablet boundary.

- Context: The mobile-lg build-time media-query threshold; CSS var() cannot parameterize a native media condition.

- Specimen kind: `breakpoint`.

##### `--breakpoint-tablet-lg`

- Purpose: The tablet-lg breakpoint supplies the wider tablet reference threshold.

- Misuse or alternative: Do not treat breakpoint-tablet-lg as a device-detection test or a promise about touch input.

## Choosing and deriving a value

Choose a semantic role before comparing numeric or color values. A chart-axis alias remains chart chrome; a density-row alias remains a sizing role; a decorative inverse ring does not become a keyboard focus indicator. Color status also needs a label or symbol, and a transparent wash must be checked on its composited ground.

Compose a one-off intermediate spacing or timing value from existing roles with calc() when the supported layout needs it. Keep a genuinely new consumer-specific decision in that consumer's own extension namespace. Do not fork this registry or add per-token inspector configuration. A newly admitted shared token must also declare one explicit display placement and its own guidance.

## Public data contract

`TOKENS`, `TOKEN_FAMILIES`, `TOKEN_GUIDANCE` and `TOKEN_DISPLAY_GROUPS` are browser-safe data. `TokenDefinition` and `TokenFamily` retain their existing shape and identity. `TokenGuidance`, `TokenApplication`, `TokenValueType`, `TokenSpecimen`, `TokenDisplayFamily` and `TokenDisplayGroup` describe the additive metadata. No React runtime or new package subpath is required.

File reading and installed-peer checks remain on `@clossys/designer/tokens/server`. See [README.md](README.md) for brand coverage, WCAG contrast, loading checks, supported CSS entry points and the complete API.

## Regenerate

```bash
node scripts/generate-token-docs.mjs # repository tooling, not shipped
node scripts/check-token-docs.mjs # repository tooling, not shipped
```

Run these repository commands after editing the source registry, guidance or navigation. The checker compares the whole document byte for byte; no installed dist, timestamps or network requests participate.
